Definition: Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses
BiblicalUsage: Two women share this name: Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz, Saul's wife, and Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, David's wife and the mother of Amnon, carried off at Ziklag and recovered by David.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no doctrine in the name. But the two Ahinoams sit on either side of the hinge of Israel's story: Saul's house going down, David's house rising, and both women caught in the turning.
RelatedPeople: King David; Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; Ahinoam, Wife of David
